registration_basis.reason: CBC and CBDV were added to the study's registered set on 2026-11-10. Both canonical identities already existed in metadata/taxonomy/compound-taxonomy.skos.jsonld (compound_cbc, compound_cbdv), so the addition reused the existing concept IDs and classifications instead of creating new ones (ISS-20261110-TAX-039). Registration fixes the query strings; it is not a substance identification.

The owner directed registration of THCB, THCP, THCJD, THCPO, HHCPO, CBND, CBL, CBGa, CBP, 10-OH-HHC, THXE and THCA on 2026-11-11. CBL and CBGa were part of that batch and are recorded separately below because the owner confirmed their intended identities the same day. Seven terms in this registration basis remain wholly UNVERIFIED: the repository has no documented chemical name, structure, class, occurrence, route/origin, synonym or regulatory evidence for them. THCP and THCJD were confirmed by the owner as isomer-unspecified homologue families - C7 (tetrahydrocannabiphorol) and C8 (THC-JD / 3-octyl-THC). For THCPO the owner confirmed only that the string means THCP-O-acetate and named no Δ8 or Δ9 isomer, so the registration is treated as an isomer-unspecified THCP-O-acetate family; that family scope is a registration-level reading of the answer, not a family the owner explicitly confirmed. None of the three is resolved to a single chemical substance or a single external record, so all three remain in the administrative category compound_identity_unverified. This category makes no route, natural occurrence, chemical-class, synonym or regulatory claim, and membership alone establishes no synonym: a concept-level alternate label (compound_thcpo's skos:altLabel `THCP-O-acetate`) records an owner-confirmed search scope with its own basis in that concept's scopeNote, not a chemical-structure equivalence. For all ten terms, registration fixes the search string only and does not establish that matching content concerns a particular substance. No synonym or identity relationship is inferred. The owner's instruction stated 17 substances but enumerated 15; the enumerated 15 are registered and no term is invented to reach 17. THCP's 2026-10-15 non-registration decision (ISS-20261015-TAX-027) is superseded for this term by the owner's 2026-11-11 scope decision; the supersession is recorded in the taxonomy scopeNote and the provenance ledger (ISS-20261111-TAX-040).

The owner confirmed on 2026-11-11 that the study term CBE is intended to mean cannabielsoin. The identity is documented against the FDA GSRS approved CANNABIELSOIN record (UNII 2ERD6V6652; CAS 52025-76-0; PubChem CID 162113; formula C21H30O3) and Wikidata Q22668702. The taxonomy concept compound_cbe is labelled Cannabielsoin (CBE) and placed in compound_minor; the source describes CBE as a non-enzymatic phytocannabinoid naturally present in Cannabis sativa (Haghdoost et al. 2024, DOI 10.3390/biomedicines12071551). The query strings `CBE` and `CBE リキッド` are unchanged: Google Trends and YouTube measure literal string matches, not verified cannabielsoin content, and existing samples are not proof of content relevance. ISS-20261111-TAX-040 addendum; docs/provenance/compound-taxonomy.md records the basis.

The owner confirmed on 2026-11-11 that the study term CBL is intended to mean cannabicyclol. The identity is documented against Wikidata Q907909 (CAS 21366-63-2, PubChem CID 30607, formula C21H30O2), the FDA GSRS record for UNII MP5WZK8M5U (names CANNABICYCLOL / CANNABIPINOL / PENTYLCANNABICYCLOL; CAS 21366-63-2, PubChem CID 59444380) and PubChem CID 59444380. PubChem CID 30607 is the stereo-unspecified record and carries CAS 67920-00-7, so no single CAS number is asserted. The taxonomy concept compound_cbl is labelled Cannabicyclol (CBL) and placed in compound_minor; the 2025 study describes CBL as a minor phytocannabinoid and reports acid-catalysed conversion from cannabichromene (Haghdoost et al. 2025, DOI 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.4c00977, PMID 39811943), and it has been quantified among phytocannabinoids in cannabis material (PMID 33839545). Neither source establishes enzymatic biosynthesis in the living plant. The query strings `CBL` and `CBL リキッド` are unchanged: the series measure literal string matches, not verified cannabicyclol content. ISS-20261111-TAX-040 addendum; docs/provenance/compound-taxonomy.md records the basis.

The owner confirmed on 2026-11-11 that the study term CBGa is intended to mean cannabigerolic acid (standard spelling CBGA). The identity is documented against ChEBI 67081, Wikidata Q27135612 (CAS 25555-57-1, PubChem CID 6449999, formula C22H32O4), the FDA GSRS record for UNII 80I4ZM847Y (names CANNABIGEROLIC ACID / CBGA) and PubChem CID 6449999. CBG is the decarboxylated product of CBGA, not a synonym (PMID 35887277). The taxonomy concept compound_cbga is labelled Cannabigerolic acid (CBGA) and placed in compound_minor. The owner's spelling `CBGa` is preserved exactly in the registered query strings `CBGa` and `CBGa リキッド`, with no case normalization in raw or query records; the series measure literal string matches, not verified cannabigerolic acid content. ISS-20261111-TAX-040 addendum; docs/provenance/compound-taxonomy.md records the basis.

On 2026-11-11 the owner confirmed that the generic chemical interpretation of THCA is replaced by three distinct search topics (Δ9-THCA-A, THCA-B, Δ8-THCA) and that of THCB by three (Δ8-THCB, Δ9-THCB, THCB-O-acetate; the acetate term is isomer-unspecified), and directed their registration (ISS-20261111-TAX-041). Each term gets the same declared query set: <term> for compound_general and <term> リキッド for product_liquid, registered active in metadata/queries/query-registry.json. The six concepts sit in the administrative registration-state category compound_identity_unverified: this change selected no single verified external record for any registered string, Δ8-THCA has no structural or nomenclatural source verified here, and THCB-O-acetate names no single isomer. The concepts therefore carry no exactMatch, no CAS/PubChem/UNII/ChEBI/Wikidata identifier, no chemical-class link and no skos:related link. The cited sources record chemistry, nomenclature and analysed products, not the content of any query result: Moreno-Sanz 2016 (DOI 10.1089/can.2016.0008); Filer 2021 (DOI 10.1089/can.2021.0003, PMCID PMC8612408); Linciano et al. 2020 (DOI 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.9b00876); Tanaka & Kikura-Hanajiri 2024 (DOI 10.1248/yakushi.24-00029); the 2024 MHLW structural groups (令和6年厚生労働省令第81号, 別紙). The generic compound_thca and compound_thcb remain separate registrations of the literal strings: their labels, notations, query IDs and adopted or preserved runs are neither reassigned nor deprecated. Registration fixes the search strings only and does not establish result-level substance identity. Current coverage is external to this design (coverage_authority).

On 2026-11-15 the owner enumerated the 27 rows of the study README's former candidate-form table (`datasets/cannabinoid-raw-collection/README.md`, now the registration-batch section) as search topics to register, and directed their registration (ISS-20261115-TAX-045). The order of the batch below is the README table's order: the six THC positional isomers, the THCP / THCJD / THCPO / THCB-O-acetate / THCH / THCV individual isomers plus the isomer-unspecified THCJD-O-acetate (13 terms), and the eight HHC stereochemical designations. Each term gets the same declared query set - `<term>` for compound_general and `<term> リキッド` for product_liquid - registered active; at registration time these queries had no run. Subsequent collection state is outside this design and is reported by coverage_authority. The evidence is not uniform and is recorded per concept rather than summarised here: registry records for Δ8-THCP, Δ9-THCP, Δ9-THCV, 9(R)-HHC and 9(S)-HHC; product analyses reported by the earlier reviews for Δ8-THCJD, Δ9-THCJD and Δ9-THCP-O-acetate; statutory structural groups (the 2024 MHLW ordinance 令和6年厚生労働省令第81号, and the Consumer Affairs Agency THCH designated-substance material) for the acetates, Δ8-THCH, Δ9-THCH and THCJD-O-acetate; the published nomenclature standard and the regulatory knowledge graph for the THC positional isomers; and the WHO 47th ECDD (2024) §2C review of eight possible HHC configurations for the six remaining stereoisomers. Two distinctions must survive downstream: a statutory structural-group listing is a legal structural fact and is not a product detection, and the WHO review of possible configurations is neither per-configuration registry evidence nor a product identification. No single verified external record was selected for any registered string, so the 27 concepts are assigned no skos:exactMatch and no CAS / PubChem CID / UNII / ChEBI / Wikidata / IUPAC identifier property, and no skos:related link, and the parent term in the candidate table (THC, THCP, THCJD, THCPO, THCB-O-acetate, THCH, THCJD, HHC, THCV) is an inventory grouping, not an asserted structural or synonym relation. THCJD-O-acetate stays the literal isomer-unspecified acetate topic: this batch does not split it into Δ8 and Δ9 rows. No historical query or run is reassigned: the generic `THC`, `THCA`, `THCB`, `THCV`, `THCH`, `HHC`, `THCP`, `THCJD`, `THCPO` and `THCB-O-acetate` queries keep their IDs, canonical texts, statuses and existing run assignments, and the generic `THC` series is not attributed to any positional isomer. The 27 terms were uncollected at registration; subsequent collection does not alter the registered query design. That state is not a zero observation. Current coverage remains external to this design and is reported by coverage_authority. Registering the 27 active compound_general queries adds 27 design-level required entries to each of the three common-scale policies (81 entries for this batch), and registering the 27 active product_liquid queries raises the required primary set from 37 to 64; those are design requirements, not collection results.

compound_set.coverage_authority: Current adopted coverage is reported by `make audit-youtube-coverage` (staging declarations + data-catalog.json) and by datasets/cannabinoid-raw-collection/README.md. This design declares the required primary set and the coverage rule; it does not carry run counts or per-term collection states. A registered primary query with no adopted run is not a zero observation, and a preserved failure (NO_DATA, HTTP 429, or NO_VIDEOS) is never converted to zero.
compound_set.coverage_rule: Two levels, both reported. Query level: a required primary query is covered when at least one adopted run carries that query_id. Compound level: a compound is complete only when all of its required primary queries are covered; some-but-not-all is `partial`, none is `missing`. One run covers only its own query_id and is never substituted for another query, and counts are never summed across queries or runs.
compound_set.identity_caveat: compound_thcnm's chemical identity is supplier/market-reported and unconfirmed. THA is an alias / commercial name of the same compound, not a second substance: both required primary queries resolve to compound_thcnm, and the two runs measure two query strings, not two substances. The query terms are the registry's canonical_text, so a run measures content matching that string, not a verified substance (ISS-20261104-TAX-028). The same caveat applies, with no single-substance identity evidence, to the seven terms registered on 2026-11-11 that remain wholly unresolved: they sit in the administrative category `compound_identity_unverified`, which makes no chemical claim (ISS-20261111-TAX-040). THCP and THCJD are a separate state: on 2026-11-11 the owner confirmed those registered strings are intended to mean the tetrahydrocannabiphorol (C7) family and the THC-JD / 3-octyl-THC (C8) family, each with the Δ8/Δ9 positional isomer unspecified. THCPO is a related but distinct state: the owner answered `y` to the confirmation question 'Does `THCPO` mean THCP-O-acetate?' and named no isomer, so the registration is treated as an isomer-unspecified THCP-O-acetate family - a registration-level reading of the answer, not an owner-confirmed family. These fix the search-topic scope only — Δ8 and Δ9 forms are distinct substances, no single external record denotes any family, the concepts carry no skos:exactMatch, and no result is attributed to an isomer — so all three stay in the same administrative category as a documented search scope (ISS-20261111-TAX-040 addendum). compound_thcpo's skos:altLabel `THCP-O-acetate` records that owner-confirmed search scope and is not a synonym for one chemical structure. CBE, CBL and CBGA are the exceptions: the owner confirmed their intended identities on 2026-11-11, and the taxonomy records the verified identifiers and places them in compound_minor. Their Google Trends / YouTube series still measure the literal `CBE` / `CBE リキッド`, `CBL` / `CBL リキッド` and `CBGa` / `CBGa リキッド` strings and do not verify the content of each result. Registration does not assert that the substance exists as the term implies. On 2026-11-11 the owner also confirmed six specific THCA/THCB search topics (ISS-20261111-TAX-041): Δ9-THCA-A, THCA-B, Δ8-THCA, Δ8-THCB, Δ9-THCB and THCB-O-acetate. Δ9-THCA-A, THCA-B, Δ8-THCB and Δ9-THCB name particular compounds in the cited literature; Δ8-THCA has no structural or nomenclatural source verified in this change; and THCB-O-acetate leaves the Δ8/Δ9 isomer unspecified. All six stay in the same administrative category without an exactMatch or identifier. The generic `THCA` and `THCB` concepts remain separate literal-string registrations, and the cited sources say nothing about the content of any result. A separate state covers the 27 forms registered on 2026-11-15 from the candidate-form table (ISS-20261115-TAX-045): they are specific positional, stereochemical or ester designations, not family-scoped terms, and they differ in evidence strength. Five carry registry records recorded by the earlier reviews, three have product analyses reported in the literature, seven rest on statutory structural groups, six on the published nomenclature standard and the regulatory knowledge graph, and six on the WHO 47th ECDD (2024) review of possible HHC configurations. None of them has a single verified external record selected for the registered string, so all 27 sit in the same administrative category without an exactMatch or identifier, and none asserts a relation to its inventory parent term. A statutory structural-group listing and a WHO configuration review are not product detections and are not query results; they are legal or review evidence about structures, recorded here so that the registration is not mistaken for a product-level finding.

query_designs.retained_out_of_scope_policy: Raw payloads and declarations for out-of-primary runs stay in place as provenance. They are excluded from primary coverage counts and are never treated as a required companion run.
query_designs.rationale: This collection observes a Japanese-market product signal, not a country-limited platform count. (a) The actor input has no geo filter. (b) The Japanese product term リキッド approximates a market restriction through the query language. (c) That approximation is not a geographic guarantee. A bare compound term is not limited to Japanese product content, so it measures a different unit and is outside the primary design.
limitations: Query-language restriction is approximate: Japanese-language content about non-Japanese markets, and non-Japanese-language content about the Japanese market, are not separated.
The actor returns a search-result sample, not a census.
Out-of-primary runs do not complete coverage for any compound.

`CBC` is also an acronym outside this domain (for example the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation), so the registered string `CBC` and `CBC リキッド` measure content matching that string, not a verified substance.

The thirteen terms registered on 2026-11-11 began as search-string registrations. Seven remain wholly unresolved and in the administrative category `compound_identity_unverified`, which asserts no route, natural occurrence, chemical class, structure, synonym or regulatory status. The owner confirmed CBE as cannabielsoin, CBL as cannabicyclol and CBGa as cannabigerolic acid on 2026-11-11; they are now documented as `compound_minor` with verified identifiers. The owner also confirmed on 2026-11-11 that `THCP` and `THCJD` denote isomer-unspecified families (C7, C8); for `THCPO` the owner confirmed only the meaning THCP-O-acetate and named no isomer, so the registration is treated as an isomer-unspecified THCP-O-acetate family. Either way that is a search-topic scope, not an isomer identification, and the Δ8/Δ9 forms are separate substances, so none of the three families carries an exactMatch (ISS-20261111-TAX-040 addendum). The two THCP-O-acetate isomers fall within the structural groups of the 2024 MHLW ordinance, subject to that ordinance's exclusion of narcotics (麻薬を除く); that is a statutory structural fact about those structures, recorded in the taxonomy and provenance ledger, and it is neither a classification of any product or query result nor part of the owner's identity confirmation, and it does not establish the content, route, occurrence, pharmacology or safety of anything returned by the queries. Even for the documented terms, runs measure content matching the literal query string, not verified substance identity or result relevance.

The THCA / THCB search topics registered on 2026-11-11 (ISS-20261111-TAX-041) split the generic chemical reading into specific strings (Δ9-THCA-A, THCA-B, Δ8-THCA; Δ8-THCB, Δ9-THCB, THCB-O-acetate). The literature documents names and, for the THCB pair, analysed products; it does not establish that any returned item concerns the named isomer or acid. Δ8-THCA has no structural or nomenclatural source verified in this change, and THCB-O-acetate names no single isomer. Registration is not an observation: this design declares required primary queries, and current coverage is reported externally.
A Google Trends attempt that returns no series (`NO_DATA`) or fails with HTTP 429 is preserved as a failed attempt, not adopted and never converted to zero.

An empty YouTube result (`NO_VIDEOS`) has no observable video dates, so it cannot yield the absolute observation window a staging declaration requires. It is preserved as an explicit marker, not adopted and not treated as a global zero.

distribution.reason: The distribution slice uses the COL-033 YouTube declaration only; this study's YouTube runs, including THCNM's, are outside that slice. compound_cbc and compound_cbdv are outside the slice because they were added to this study's registered set on 2026-11-10 and are not part of COL-033. The thirteen terms registered on 2026-11-11 (ISS-20261111-TAX-040) are outside the slice for the same reason. The seven whose identity remains wholly unverified, plus `compound_thcp`, `compound_thcjd` and `compound_thcpo` whose owner-confirmed scope is an isomer-unspecified family rather than a substance, may not enter a release even after collection; CBE, CBL and CBGA — whose identity is documented — also stay outside the slice unless a separate release decision adds them. Registering a compound does not widen the slice. The six THCA / THCB search-topic concepts registered on 2026-11-11 (ISS-20261111-TAX-041) are outside the slice for the same reason; none has a release decision, and Δ8-THCA and THCB-O-acetate do not identify a single substance. Registering them does not widen the slice.
